overview: Globant is a Luxembourg-incorporated, NYSE-listed IT services and digital engineering company founded in Buenos Aires in 2003, providing software development, design, and AI-enabled digital transformation services to large enterprises. The company organizes delivery around 'Studios' (technology/domain practices), 'Agile Pods' (self-organized delivery teams), and increasingly 'AI Pods' sold as a subscription/output-based model through its Globant Enterprise AI (Glob.AI) platform. It operates through roughly 27,400 employees ('Globers') across 30+ countries, with revenue concentrated in North America (~53%), Latin America (~21%) and Europe (~21%), serving blue-chip clients such as Google, Electronic Arts, Santander and Disney.

business_model.summary: Globant monetizes primarily through time-and-materials and fixed-price IT/software engineering contracts billed per engineer-hour or project milestone (the traditional 'seats' model), supplemented by a fast-growing subscription/consumption-based AI Pods offering priced on output rather than hours. Revenue is project- and relationship-based rather than contractually recurring, though long-tenured top accounts (some 10+ years, e.g., Disney, EA) create de facto recurring demand. The core business remains a people-intensive staffing/delivery model monetizing nearshore/offshore Latin American and global engineering talent at a blended bill-rate markup over (largely local-currency) labor cost.

revenue_streams.name: Traditional IT services / staff-augmentation & project delivery (Studios, Agile Pods, time-and-materials + fixed-price)
AI Pods / Glob.AI platform (subscription, output/consumption-based pricing)

business_model.customer_type: B2B enterprise; large global corporates and '100-squared' strategic accounts across banking/financial services, media & entertainment, consumer/retail/manufacturing, travel & hospitality, and technology/telecom
business_model.geographic_mix: North America ~52.8%, Latin America ~20.8% (top country Argentina), Europe ~20.9% (top country Spain), New Markets (Asia/Oceania/Middle East) ~5.5% (Q2 2026); ~63% of revenue billed in USD, remainder in local currencies (notably Colombian peso, Brazilian real, Mexican peso) creating a cost-base/revenue-base currency mismatch since delivery costs are predominantly LatAm-currency-denominated

main_competitors: Indian IT majors (TCS, Infosys, Wipro, Cognizant)
competitive_position.market_position: Mid-cap pure-play digital engineering/AI-native services provider; smaller and more AI/design-centric than Accenture or Capgemini, competes most directly with EPAM and Endava for 'born-digital' enterprise transformation work; distinguishes itself from Indian IT majors via LatAm nearshore delivery, cultural/time-zone proximity to US/European clients, and a design-and-innovation-led (not purely cost-arbitrage) value proposition

moat_factors.description: 10+ year relationships with marquee accounts (Disney, EA, Google) and a growing cohort of 20 accounts over $20M/year provide embedded, hard-to-displace delivery relationships

moat_factors.factor: LatAm nearshore talent pool and time-zone/cultural alignment with North America
moat_factors.description: Historically a structural cost and proximity advantage over offshore India-based competitors for US/European clients requiring close collaboration

moat_factors.factor: AI-native delivery brand and partnerships (Anthropic, OpenAI, Vercel)
moat_factors.description: Early mover positioning around agentic AI/AI Pods and the Glob.AI platform, but moat is unproven at scale and the entire model is still ~4% of revenue
Differentiated delivery model (Studios, Agile Pods, 'Stay Relevant') built up over two decades, but increasingly commoditized as AI coding tools compress the value of pure engineering staffing

weaknesses: Core business model (billing by the hour/headcount) is directly threatened by generative AI productivity tools that reduce the engineering hours clients need to buy
High client concentration: top 10 clients ~30.6% of revenue, top client alone ~8.9%
Customer count shrinking (904 LTM customers vs 981 a year earlier; >$1M accounts down to 331 from 339)
Smaller scale than Accenture/Capgemini/TCS limits ability to win the largest enterprise-wide transformation mandates
Recent credibility damage from the 2023-2025 'Latin America pivot' failure and resulting securities class action impairs trust in management's guidance and disclosures

Heavy reliance on Latin American cost base (especially Colombia) exposed to local-currency appreciation against USD-denominated revenue, which management says cost ~4 points of margin over the last two years

growth_drivers: AI Pods / Glob.AI platform: ARR grew from $20.6M (Q4 2025) to $32.8M (Q1 2026) to $52.8M (Q2 2026), with management guiding to a $110M+ exit run-rate by year-end 2026 and expecting ~4% of FY2026 revenue; carries ~10 points higher gross margin than traditional delivery

Glob.AI platform opened to the broader market (not just existing clients) in August 2026, with partnerships with Anthropic, Vercel and OpenAI, targeting a larger professional-services TAM beyond traditional IT services
Expansion within top accounts: top-50 clients grew revenue 6.9% YoY even as overall revenue was flat, suggesting wallet-share gains inside the largest relationships
Large enterprise AI-transformation deals in energy, sports and gaming verticals highlighted by management as evidence of '100-squared' account strategy working
Pipeline reported at over $3 billion (as of Q4 2025) and $436.8 million specifically for AI-related engagements (Q2 2026), providing forward revenue visibility if conversion holds
Continued (though now more selective) tuck-in M&A to add capabilities/geographies, historically a core part of Globant's growth playbook
Record free cash flow generation (H1 2026 was the strongest first half on record) funding an active buyback program ($125M authorization)

business.risk: GenAI disruption of the staff-augmentation model
business.description: AI coding assistants and agentic AI reduce the number of billable engineering hours enterprises need to buy; management is deliberately cannibalizing its own time-and-materials revenue by migrating clients to lower-revenue, higher-margin AI Pods, which is depressing top-line growth in the near term with no guarantee of a smooth transition

Top 10 clients ~30.6% of revenue; loss or budget pullback at a handful of large accounts can move consolidated results materially, as seen in Middle East project delays and travel/hospitality slowdowns in 2026

business.risk: Shrinking customer base and project cancellations
business.description: LTM customers served fell from 981 to 904 and $1M+ accounts fell from 339 to 331 over the year to Q2 2026, reflecting both AI-driven efficiency and genuine demand softness

business.risk: Reputational/credibility damage from the failed Latin America pivot
business.description: 2023-2025 disclosures revealed deteriorating LatAm demand, client defections and a problematic Iteris (Brazil) acquisition that management had allegedly downplayed, raising the bar of skepticism around current AI-pivot narrative

financial.risk: LatAm currency appreciation vs. USD revenue
financial.description: ~37% of revenue is non-USD while the cost base is concentrated in Latin American currencies (particularly Colombian peso); management states FX appreciation cost ~4 points of margin over the trailing two years

financial.risk: One-time Business Optimization Costs recurring across periods
financial.description: $47.6M (Q2 2025), $32.3M (Q2 2026) and a further $20-25M guided for Q3 2026 in restructuring charges (workforce resizing, office consolidation) are compressing IFRS margins well below adjusted/non-IFRS margins and raise questions about whether these are truly 'one-time'

Non-current borrowings increased from $347.0M (Dec-2025) to $402.6M (Jun-2026) while cash fell, partly funding buybacks amid declining operating cash generation per quarter versus prior guidance expectations

regulatory.description: Multiple law firms filed securities fraud class actions (lead plaintiff deadline June 23, 2026) alleging Globant and executives made false/misleading statements about the Latin American pivot between February 2024 and August 2025, concealing client defections and declining demand; outcome and potential damages/settlement are unresolved
Operates under preferential tax/promotion regimes in Argentina, Uruguay, India and Belarus; changes, non-renewal or tightening of these regimes would raise the effective tax rate and operating costs

regulatory.risk: Data privacy and IP regulation across 30+ countries
regulatory.description: Exposure to a patchwork of data protection, labor and IP regimes given global delivery footprint

macro.description: Historical exposure to Argentine peso devaluation, capital controls, export duties on services and high inflation; while reduced vs. a decade ago, the delivery base remains concentrated in Argentina, Colombia, Brazil, Mexico and Uruguay

Discretionary technology spending is sensitive to macro slowdowns; 2026 guidance already reflects elongated North American decision cycles and travel/hospitality client pullback tied to oil-price volatility
Rising borrowings and a professional-services business model with limited fixed assets give it low direct balance-sheet rate sensitivity but higher finance expense as debt grows

macro_factors.industry_outlook: Global IT services/digital engineering spend continues to grow overall, but 2025-2026 has seen a structural de-rating of the sector as investors price in AI-driven price deflation and demand disintermediation; traditional staff-augmentation economics are under genuine pressure while 'AI-native' delivery models are unproven at scale
macro_factors.cyclicality: Moderate-to-high - enterprise technology/digital-transformation budgets are discretionary and contract in downturns or during periods of CFO caution, as evidenced by 2026 guidance softness
macro_factors.interest_rate_sensitivity: Low-to-moderate direct exposure; indirect sensitivity via client capital budgets and via Globant's own growing borrowings
key_input_costs: Latin American engineering/IT labor costs and wage inflation
Foreign exchange rates (ARS, COP, BRL, MXN, EUR vs. USD)
Cloud/compute and AI-model licensing costs for Glob.AI platform delivery

recent_developments.event: Revenue $614.4M, essentially flat YoY ($614.2M prior year); $32.3M Business Optimization Cost charge compressed IFRS operating margin to 3.2% (vs 1.0% a year earlier, but far below the historical ~9% run-rate); non-IFRS adjusted operating margin fell to 13.2% from 15.0%

Stock fell ~12% after FY2026 revenue guidance was cut to $2.428-$2.462B, implying -1.1% to +0.3% YoY growth; multiple analysts (Wedbush, Guggenheim, Goldman Sachs, TD Cowen) cut price targets, with Wedbush downgrading to Neutral

Glob.AI ARR reached $52.8M, up 61% QoQ from $32.8M in Q1 2026; Globant opened the Glob.AI platform to the broader market (not just existing clients), partnering with Anthropic, Vercel and OpenAI, and raised its year-end ARR exit target to $110M+

Headcount fell to 27,411 Globers (down ~9-10% YoY) as the company reduces traditional delivery staff and reskills remaining teams toward higher-value data/cloud/AI-implementation work; revenue per employee rose ~9.7% YoY
New $125 million share repurchase program authorized after completing the prior $125M program; insider buying reported (director purchase of 25,000 shares, ~$971,750, May 2026)

Securities class action lawsuits filed (multiple firms) alleging Globant misled investors about the health of its Latin American operations and the 2023 'Latin America pivot' between Feb-2024 and Aug-2025; lead plaintiff deadline was June 23, 2026
Revenue $607.1M, down 0.7% YoY but above the high end of guidance; record H1 free cash flow; management cited 'AI Pods are the engine' of a pivot beyond the traditional seats model

FY2025 revenue $2,454.9M (+1.6% YoY), the highest in company history, with record quarterly free cash flow of $152.8M; however FY2025 IFRS operating margin fell to 7.0% from 9.3% in FY2024 due to Business Optimization Costs; guidance issued for FY2026 implying only 0.2-2.2% growth (since cut further)

Stock declined from a 2025 high of ~$210 to roughly $66 by August 2025 across three corrective disclosures (Feb, May, Aug 2025) tied to deteriorating Latin American demand, ~1,000 employee cuts and a $47.6M restructuring charge, the precursor to the 2026 securities litigation

items.notes: Implies -1.1% to +0.3% YoY growth including a 70bp positive FX tailwind; down from the $2,462-$2,508M range (0.3%-2.2% growth) guided just one quarter earlier at Q1 2026

items.metric: Non-IFRS Adjusted Profit from Operations Margin
items.notes: Down from the 14.0-15.0% range guided at Q1 2026; FY2025 actual was 15.2%
Down from $6.10-$6.50 guided at Q1 2026; assumes ~43.6 million average diluted shares; FY2025 actual adjusted diluted EPS was $6.14
Represents a 1.6% YoY decline to 0.3% YoY decline, including a 25bp positive FX impact

items.metric: Non-IFRS Adjusted Profit from Operations Margin (Q3 2026)
items.notes: A further ~$20-25M of Business Optimization Costs is expected in Q3 2026 on top of this adjusted margin
Raised from a prior $60-100M exit-ARR framing after ARR reached $52.8M in Q2 2026, up 61% QoQ; management expects AI Pods to reach ~4% of FY2026 revenue

guidance.management_commentary: CEO Martín Migoya framed the quarter as proof of a deliberate pivot to an 'AI-native tech services' and output/consumption-based pricing model via Glob.AI and AI Pods, acknowledging the company is 'accelerating these migrations, even if it means a short-term impact on revenue.' CFO Juan Urthiague said the company 'proactively optimized our structure during the quarter to navigate broader market volatility and align with our business model transformation needs,' citing currency appreciation in Latin America (~4 points of margin headwind over two years, concentrated in Colombia) and attributing the FY2026 guidance cut to unexpected Middle East project delays, oil-price-driven travel/hospitality slowdowns, and elongated North American decision cycles. Management expects the AI Pod transition to 're-accelerate' growth, with Migoya suggesting a 'pretty strong effect' could show by the end of 2027.

bull_case: AI Pods/Glob.AI is scaling fast off a small base (ARR +61% QoQ to $52.8M) with ~10 points higher gross margin than legacy delivery, and management has already raised its year-end ARR target once this year, suggesting the platform could become a real second growth engine

Record free cash flow generation (strongest H1 on record) funds an active buyback ($125M program) at a materially de-rated valuation (~$35/share vs a 2025 high near $210 and 13.9x trailing P/E), with insider buying also reported

Deep, multi-year relationships with marquee enterprise clients (Disney, EA, Google, Santander) and continued wallet-share expansion in top-50 accounts (+6.9% YoY) even as total revenue stalls, suggesting the best clients are not fleeing

Management is self-cannibalizing the legacy time-and-materials model proactively rather than being disrupted passively, which — if the transition is executed well — could leave Globant ahead of slower-moving competitors in pricing software-like output rather than hours

Restructuring actions (headcount down ~9-10% YoY, revenue per employee up ~9.7%) are already improving productivity metrics, and management guides to H2 2026 margin recovery as Business Optimization Costs roll off
bear_case: The core business model — billing enterprise clients by engineer-hours — is structurally threatened by generative AI coding tools that reduce the hours needed, and it is not obvious Globant's AI Pods revenue can replace lost time-and-materials revenue dollar-for-dollar, as the current guidance cut illustrates

Credibility risk: the 2023-2025 'Latin America pivot' episode (stock fell from ~$210 to ~$66, ~1,000 jobs cut, now the subject of an active securities fraud class action) shows management has previously been slow to disclose deteriorating fundamentals, raising doubt about how much of the current 'temporary market dislocation' framing is accurate versus more structural

Repeated, recurring 'one-time' Business Optimization Costs across three consecutive quarters ($47.6M, then more in 2026, with a further $20-25M guided for Q3 2026) suggest the restructuring is ongoing and margin troughs may persist longer than management signals

Shrinking customer base (LTM customers served down from 981 to 904, $1M+ accounts down from 339 to 331) and client concentration (top 10 ~30.6% of revenue) leave results vulnerable to further project cancellations or budget pullbacks, as already seen in the Middle East and travel/hospitality verticals

FX headwinds from LatAm currency appreciation against a largely USD-denominated revenue base are structural to the delivery model and have already cost ~4 points of margin over two years, with no clear mechanism to fully hedge given the labor-cost nature of the exposure
